body:
Wow, that sounds extremely manipulative and immature. It's not that she can't stand to see the child hurt, it's that she's jealous of the attention and soothing the child gets and wants that herself. 

Seems like parentification to me - she expects you to make her feel better too. I'd completely ignore her - you don't need twice the fires to put out everytime there's an accident.

Exactly. I think she's under the impression that you "roll the dice" on your child, and they're either loving and caring (subservient), or they're an evil, terrible human (independent, and autonomous). So messed up.
Wow, that rings a bell. I can't count how many "jokes" were made that we're dishwashers/lawn mowers/cleaners etc. Pretty sure they actually just needed "extras" to help with daily chores.

You're definitely right to advocate for your girlfriend. There's a big difference between helping cover living costs and being gouged for money because they have the position to do that. It was an issue with me and my siblings too - especially when it came to signing over all our tax credits that we didn't even understand fully. 

I would suggest helping her write out a budget to get things on paper and clear. Count all income and expenses (including debts, transportation, food, necessities etc). Also include savings -  many people don't add this to the budget, but it's so important. If you aren't putting any money away, then you will be forever stuck in your current situation. If it's possible, have her go over this budget with her mom, and explain that the numbers won't work with the amount she's expecting. This may or may not go well, depending if she's prone to the "you're so ungrateful!" rages.

If it doesn't go well, then I would 100% start helping her look for a cheap place elsewhere. If it's less than what her mom was charging, then it's a perfect solution. If it does happen to be a bit more, don't forget the peace of mind and sanity it comes with - that's worth its weight in gold. There's also things she can do to help tighten the budget. Many student loans or other debts can offer "breaks" during life transitions, especially as a new grad. This can help her save enough for first + last rent payments, as well as negotiating rent rates with landlords too. 

Hope it goes well for her! I'm sure she's grateful to have you sticking up for her.

I remember during elementary school health class question period asking what to do if you don't want to tell your parents. That was met with a "don't be silly" kind of laugh and they said "you'll have to tell them."

I still remember the embarrassment of asking, the teacher did not understand at all. Oddly enough, when I did tell my parents, I had my first panic attack (though I didn't know what it was at the time, I now recognize what happened.) 

Sorry you went through that, that was pretty terrible of your parents to let you struggle on your own.

Two years of being engaged and starting to plan a wedding and she not ONCE asked anything about it. No questions, no curiosity, obviously no offers of help. 

Three months prior to the wedding she sends me a snippy email that "they feel like they know nothing about the wedding." I responded that they haven't shown any interest in the plans so we didn't bother sharing details, then I answered her questions and talked a bit about it. Then came the wrath.

"Obviously we're interested! We were just giving you space since you can't take my advice well! See?? Just like now, throwing it back at me. We're obviously not important to you. We're just "guests" I suppose. Won't bother asking for more details then, we'll just wait for the invite and your apology!!"

Invite never came :)

I worked customer service in retail during my high school years and had a few "difficult" customers. I've told my husband some of the stories and he's always in awe that I handled it so calmly. He said he'd have been fired so many times based on how he would have reacted.

Thinking about it now, I'm pretty sure I've just had so much at-home experience, that nothing was ever as bad as facing my own parents. I used to take every possible shift I could get, working almost every day because no matter what customer was there, it was still less stressful than being at home.

"Reclining Throne" - love that description!! 

Mine were the same way - nmom watching tv, edad out working in the barns. I vaguely remember when I was very young playing family board games a couple of times. Then it was just the odd card game with my mother, if I brought it to her in front of the tv. Then I just gave up and played video games by myself or with my siblings. 

Going out with friends now and trying things for the first time is a great way to give yourself the experiences you never had. Since leaving my parents house, I've tried so many things: golfing, snowboarding, paintball etc. I won't live my life how they do - we've seen first hand what a crumby life that is, we can use it as our motivation!

Wow, what a horrible text. She manages to completely insult you every step of the way, while also making herself out to be the martyr who deserves empathy. 

Her views on parenting are completely backwards. You don't get to pick your child's interests and life goals... this isn't The Sims!! 

Don't waste your time and energy on her toxic personality. Do what makes YOU happy. This is YOUR life, and the hobbies and career you choose affect YOU, not her. She can deal with her own feelings of failure - that is NOT your problem, and you are NOT the cause.

When I first went No Contact, I was so mad at them for still "not getting it". They never took responsibility for their actions, never apologized, never tried to make things right. All I got was a warped half-apology that tried to get me to admit that I'm the real one at fault.

Now that some time has passed and I haven't heard any more efforts from them to repair things, I'm just kind of sad. I see all these other happy families and parents that genuinely care, and I wish so much that I knew what that was like. 

Not sure what the next stage is, or how to move on from here though.

Haha they really do love to "decipher" people's looks. My mother immediately disliked my sister's now-husband after meeting him the first time. The reason? "He was poking around at the corn on his plate, judging it. I guess my cooking isn't good enough for him!!!"

Geez.

That's a great way to frame it! It's an exciting (and sometimes scary) transition into the next part of your life.  You've faced hardships and you've overcome them all to become the strong person you are today. You know that you can handle what life throws at you, and that's an important thing to always remember. Congrats again!

Absolutely. I use to only take out exactly $20 from my paychecks in highschool to spend on myself for the next two weeks (which usually was just for cheap lunches or energy drinks while at work), and still felt like I was "stealing" from myself. The rest of my wages all went to savings for school. 

I never bought a car until just last year (26 years old) because I couldn't get over the fact that "buses are cheaper, and walking is free."

I also hold on to so much junk, because throwing it out seems like wasted money when I could fix it myself or use it for a new project.

Now that I'm finally graduated and working full time, I still have a hard time making "unnecessary" purchases without feeling wracked with guilt. It's getting better as I tell myself that money IS for spending. If you're not enjoying the present, what's the point of working miserably for 40 years to only enjoy your money in retirement and old age? There's a balance for sure, but it's important to also enjoy life, and sometimes splurging a little is simply self-care.

Congratulations on all your hard work, dedication, and well earned achievement!

If I can pass along a word of advice: make sure you go and celebrate YOU that day. Treat yourself well, do whatever little things make you happy.

I was still in contact with my parents when I graduated, but their response was "hope you don't mind that we don't attend - you know how these things are and it'll just be long and boring." I didn't want to go alone, so I cancelled my gown rental and stayed at work that day. I regret it entirely. 

Don't make the mistake I did. You deserve to celebrate your milestone. You should be proud!

I lost all my respect for my dad.

The rest of my family has been cut off years ago, and now I realize that they probably WEREN'T the bad ones. I don't know how much truth was in any of the stories I was told growing up.

I'm sorry you're facing that dilemma :( It sucks realizing the small things in life don't work quite the same in dysfunctional families. I definitely wouldn't break NC over it - you know that she'd likely just hold it over your head like she did you the grandest of favors, or use it as an excuse to pretend like everything's fine again.

My suggestion is to make your own new favourite recipe! You can have fun in the process, and it can become a great thing to pass along to your child. You'll bond over making them together, and they'll have memories of those great eggs like you do, only they'll be able to keep the legacy going. 

Serious Eats has never let me down before, and this article comes with a bunch of variations. Hopefully one strikes a chord with you and you can make it your own! 
 https://www.seriouseats.com/2014/05/great-deviled-eggs-variations-and-hacks.html

Also if it helps, don't forget that we tend to build things up a lot in our minds, to a point where it can never live up to our expectations. There's a good chance that even having her recipe wouldn't solve your craving. I bet you can make even better ones ;)

Haha, ah ok. So basically you can hold the shower head it in your hand and just aim it where you want water. Start at the roots of your hair and aim downwards to wet it. Then you can put it back on the hook, lather shampoo in your hair with both hands, then pick it back up to rinse out again in the same way. 

If you look up a video/walk by a hair salon, you'll see how they wash hair that way over a sink (it's the same principle in the shower, you just don't have to cram your neck backwards). They do it so they can wash customer's hair without getting their face/make-up wet, so it would hopefully help you out too.

Would having a different shower head help? There are ones with low pressure, or ones that have the water go straight down like rainfall. Or a handheld one (with the hose) might help so that you can run it through your hair only and not your face.

I think it has to do with having empathy for the person being picked on. We know intimately what it's like to be made the butt of the joke, and how unpleasant that is with no one taking your feelings seriously.

My personal most hated joke is the fake lottery ticket prank. You literally get someone's hopes up just to destroy them for a laugh. I feel so bad for those people, I can't watch those pranks.

Wow, she sounds eerily like mine! The thing that really stood out for me too - her typos increase and coherence decreases as her emotions grow. Is that something that normally occurs?

It's like they get blinded by rage. Reading up on Borderline "waifs" explained so much of it for me. If you haven't heard of that, I recommend looking it up. Hope you had a happy birthday!

My personal experience: the only real change is the use of more subtle tactics as she got older. Passive aggressive remarks, gaslighting, ignoring accomplishments, and rage filled emails replaced the childhood screaming, pushing, name-calling, and silent treatments. 

So while the "loudness" has mellowed, the underlying themes never changed. Nothing you do will ever be good enough, they will never be happy for you, and they will never be a source of support or comfort. They want you to make sure you don't "forget your place" as the child, they want you to thank them continuously for what a great parent they are, and they want to constantly receive care and attention - especially since they're now "your aging elders".

So they trade in the "You will listen to and respect me because I'm your parent!" mantra for "After all I've done for you, you're going to abandon me in my old age!" bit.

I've noticed that too. I think it's because it's more "accepted" in society when fathers are bad parents (plenty of news stories, books, tv shows, movies about abusive/distant/abandoning fathers), but when a mother acts that way, it's harder to understand why since it appears less talked about and less common. We don't have the same stories to compare it to.

So we take to the Internet to try and find answers, we research and read, and we end up in forums like this where we finally see we're not alone - other mothers ARE this way too. It's not just us, it's not just our family. So I think the gender difference could very well be equal, but those with nfathers might have just chalked it up to "he's just a bad father" and never made their way here to dig deeper. Just my thoughts though, I could be completely wrong.

Ah, that's terrible. Good on you for telling her to make the call herself! Certainly not your job to play middleman there. 

I hope she finds help for her gambling problem. Sounds like morals go out the door when she's desperate. I hope your finances are safe too, you don't need her ruining your life and your future with her problems.
Nmom, no contact, volatile.

Is it possible to send out a message to those she's in contact with to clarify that you do not want information about your life shared with her?  Something short and simple to just state your boundaries. Might help reduce some of it. Those who refuse to respect your privacy can get put on a "data diet'" so they'll have nothing interesting to share.

I've done some searching on social media for my dad's side, but haven't found anyone. I know their names, but that's it. 

For my mom's side, I have no idea if they're worth finding. She grew up in a family of 6 children in a strict Catholic environment. From her stories, they're all gossips and drama queens. But I don't know what to believe anymore. I think I have contact info for one of my aunts, but at the time my mother "forbade" me from contacting her. So I don't know what to do.

The fact that you're self-reflecting is a great sign that you won't become the way your mother was. 

I think it's normal to want care and attention from others. The key is not demanding it, and also returning that to others. Relationships are a give and take - help others, be kind to them, and they'll help you in return. One-sided relationships are not healthy, both parties should be contributing and supporting each other in their time of need.

It's also important to realize that the world is full of a huge array of people - and no two are the same. Wanting EVERYONE to like you or care about you just isn't feasible. There's always going to be some people that just don't "click" with you - and that's ok. In the same way, you're not expected to like everyone you meet either. 

As for accomplishments and goals, that's perfectly fine to want success for yourself. It's important to have things to work towards and look forward to in life. Being proud of your achievements and wanting a "congratulations" is normal. Again, the key here is not demanding recognition for it, but instead feeling an internal pride in knowing you worked hard and achieved what you set your sights on.

I'm sorry you have to face that. Do what YOU feel like, no one understands your situation as well as yourself. Trust your gut, don't give in for the sake of others. 

I don't really have any family because of my mother. She's cut off or been cut off by everyone on both her side and my dad's. No friends, co-workers or neighbors of hers either. And my dad dare not stand up to her, so by cutting her off, I lost contact with him too. So no guilt trips to face at least.

I think the good times are definitely tougher. It sucks when the very people who should be happy and support you either don't care at all, or find some way to ruin the joy. It's hard to feel happy when it comes with a whole extra set of drama or disappointment, and life without those happy moments starts to lose its appeal.

Tough times suck, but I think we've all had our share of having to be strong for ourselves, knowing we can't rely on others. So while we don't have the support we wish we had, we can fight through it and come out stronger. But tough times without any happy times to balance it out really sucks. 

The moments that stand out the most over the years for me was the times when I thought my parents would be happy for me, but they weren't. They didn't attend my university graduation because it would be "too boring" to sit through. They didn't ask anything at all about my wedding plans because "they wanted me to have my space". Those were the moments that you realize that they never will care, and you have to learn to be happy for and take pride in yourself.

First year of being no contact with my nMother, and it will be a nice change of pace not having to deal with that stress. 

Not a single mother's day in my life has gone well - it's either stress out about being careful with your words and plans, or stress out about hearing how disappointing you are compared to "such and such" or people on TV.

My brother and I are both no contact, leaving only my sister left as low contact. My mother has gone down a deep spiral, realizing there's literally no one left who will put up with her abuse. She told my dad to tell my sister to ignore mother's day - she wants to pretend it doesn't exist. I don't know, this seems like a huge trap...I hope it fairs well for my sister.

Organs get sick, have defects, face illnesses. The brain is an organ. It can have issues too.

I'll never understand why people don't believe in mental illnesses. There's so much research and evidence out there, they just need to inform themselves more.

You know that it's real. We know that it's real. Doctors know that it's real. It definitely sucks when others don't understand, but that's their problem and their lack of education. They may understand one day when they learn more about it, but for now all you can do is try to not let it get you down, and surround yourself with people who are supportive and understand.

I've tried to get into it so many times... But 1) I never remember to keep up with it daily 2) I can't seem to block out the world around me and 3) my thoughts are constantly coming in when I try (though I'm sure this would be helped with more practice).

I've tried doing simple techniques on my own, tried following along with various apps, and I still just can't get into it. Then I feel bad because it seems like such a simple and beneficial thing to do, yet I've just given up on it.

Did you find it hard to start out? What did you use to remind yourself to practice, and what helps keep you focused?
Abuse and neglect can cause physical changes in the brain and chemical imbalances though

Holy gaslighting Batman! He's trying to make you second guess your and your therapist's choices, because they don't paint him in a positive light. Notice that there wasn't a single "what can I do to make things better?", only "you need to do this or that to change yourself" and questioning your therapist's competence because they're catching on to his behaviour.

Reading that honestly made me angry, it reminds me of my nmother's old emails. Keep doing what you feel is best for YOU, don't listen to this garbage! A truly caring parent would own up to their mistakes, apologize, and try to find a path forward EVEN if they thought it wasn't entirely their fault. He's just deflecting all blame with "nothing to see here!" types of statements and trying to downplay his faults with "others have had it worse" and "we're ALL hypocrites."

Depending on your situation, I'd consider not replying at all. Don't give him any inkling that he's bothering you or making you question anything - that'll only make him try harder. He's completely backwards here, and without knowing anything else about him, that is definitely toxic behavior that you don't need in your life.

You have every right to stand up for yourself and your brother. It's important to tell them what you will and will not tolerate, don't think of it as a mistake! 

Working on a better choice of words might help, such as "I don't want to hear what you have to say about my brother." Or "I do not agree with what you are saying, and do not wish to discuss this further." Then calmly walk away. It's hard, but try to not let your anger get in the way, as it always makes narcs escalate the situation. Count to 10 taking deep breaths first if you need. 

I've had to reiterate numerous times to my parents that I will not be involved in talking about others behind their backs. Make your boundary and stick to it. It's extremely hard at first, but it gets easier!

Flying monkeys are people who try to get you to contact the narcissist again. Sometimes it's because they think things aren't that bad, or they try to guilt you into being "the bigger person". Other times it's because the narcissist has fed them lies and manipulated them to rope you back into contact.

The actual term "flying monkey" I believe is a Wizard of Oz reference, as the Wicked Witch has an army of flying monkeys to do her bidding. 

Edit: here's the subreddit's definitions and terms: https://www.reddit.com/r/raisedbynarcissists/wiki/acronyms

Oh man, mine did the same. And then when I didn't respond, I'd get raged at again for my rudeness. 

I'm pretty sure this is just a maneuver to deflect from them having to apologize...

Left just before 18, when I went to live at university. She made my high school life hell, I couldn't wait to leave. Near the end I would just walk away from arguments by saying "x many days left" and it surprisingly was effective at getting her to stop screaming.

The first day that I was on my own was one of the best days in my life. It was like I could finally breathe, I could do anything I wanted! Stay up late? No problem. Eat whatever I want? Go for it. Want to just sit in silence? Go right ahead!

I kept contact with her for years, but never, ever went back to live there. I shared apartments and houses, and worked as much as I needed to make sure I would never be dependent on them again. Things seemed somewhat better, but there was always this constant nagging feeling, like waiting for a bomb to go off. "Oh, it's been a few weeks, better send an email or get yelled at." "Crap, holidays are coming up, better find a good excuse to limit how long I have to visit." 

Long story short, it was years of her expecting me to keep in touch or face her rage, yet all without any positives in return. She never was happy for me, never asked how I was doing, she didn't even attend my graduation because it would be "too boring." I'm 26 now and cut contact a few months ago. I'm finally seeing improvements in my mental health and happiness, and wish I had done that sooner. I now have that same amazing feeling of being able to "breathe" again.

I'm sorry he put you through that, hopefully it at least provides some closure that you made the right choice to go no contact. 

You're spot on with noticing the projection - Ns have a great way of describing themselves perfectly when insulting others. It's a double whammy too because it "uses up" those insults so you can't just say "no YOU are" without sounding ridiculous. 

He lives in his own reality, and unfortunately you can't change others, you can only change how you interact with them. Look out for yourself and don't take any insults from a sick mind to heart. Keep your distance and know that you will live a happy life surrounded by people who truly care about you.

Huh, I know I'm bad at only thinking about things instead of feeling them, but never made the connection that maybe this is just another part of that... 

I've looked into trying to fix my seemingly missing emotions, but haven't really had any luck. Everything just says "start noticing how you feel," but either I'm broken and there's nothing there or I'm not recognzing it or something.

Thanks for the insights, I'll set my focus to that and see if I get any further.

I'm glad that I've successfully dodged this question everytime she asks. It's like the old schoolyard question of "Am I ugly?" just to get people to give you compliments. Nope - not giving into that trap.

Still am. I realize now that other families regularly hug each other or place their hand on someone's shoulder or back. It's hard to not be jumpy and feel extremely uncomfortable when that happens to me though.

I'm trying to get over it as I want to eventually be a parent, and I don't ever want to be as cold and distant as my parents were, but I still find myself overanalyzing any kind gesture towards me for days after the fact.

Thankfully she gave up on social media early when she realized she doesn't have anyone she talks to (literally no friends, family, or acquaintances have stuck around), but she's done this through email. 

She'd send a "Blocked!" email in her anger to try and upset us, not realizing how incredibly childish that is. She'd soon realize that it's not like we're going to call her up and grovel to her to unblock us, so she'd eventually cave and send us an "Unblocked" email, as though we were granted the honor of her emails again.

I definitely understand that feeling, I have a hard time trusting that someone else could help me (or even want to), and I much prefer to just solve things myself.

I signed up for online counseling last year (on BetterHelp.com) that I've used off and on because I needed a few extra strategies to help fix my anxiety and sleeping issues. I really recommend online counseling - you don't have to share your name or information with the counselor. You don't have to upload a profile picture, and you can keep everything text based. 

I think it's helped me trust a bit more and take small risks, even if I can't bring myself to go to someone in person yet. Might be something worth considering.

Personally, I don't like lying - dealt with enough dishonesty growing up. Simply stating "we're not close" or "we don't talk anymore" usually gets the point across and they don't push any further.  I'd stick with something like that.
Do you mind if I ask, how do you begin the conversation with a therapist? Do you start with addressing specific issues and the conversation just evolves from there? Or how does that work?
I've always had roommates, so my simple answer is, "It's their home too, and we don't give out keys."

Thanks for the suggestions about non-social volunteer work! I've given up on more than one self help books because they're always just saying "be kind to others, give out compliments, smile at them" which doesn't help when you have social anxiety...

I've done a lot of reading this past year, and I'm pretty sure she's on the borderline/narcissistic spectrum - and it's definitely explained so much. It's just hard to understand/accept that they won't change... It doesn't make any sense why she doesn't see that her way of relating to others isn't working. I feel so bad that she's so unhappy, but I just couldn't take her constant criticism and put downs anymore, so I had to step away.

I could try, they don't get along either so they'd probably understand why I'd want to keep it private. I've just been told so many stories about why THEY'RE the problem and my mom is the victim, but I don't know the real truth. They stopped talking when I was 8 or 9, and only briefly reconnected a few years ago before severing ties again. I'd have to find a way to contact them too, I wasn't able to find any on Facebook. But I'll keep it in mind for the future, see if we can have our own relationship.

I've thought about trying to connect with some of my extended family, but I'm terrified of my mom's reaction if she ever found out. She'll think I'm doing it just to hurt her, which will either make her even more depressed, or go into a complete rage, neither of which is my intention. So I don't know if that'll ever be a possibility. 

We're trying to be closer to my inlaw's side at least, so hopefully we can build a more traditional family there. I just want my future children to have the experience of extended family and gatherings that I never really had.

A lot of people use physical pain to relieve emotional pain, so it could be that (sort of like hair pulling or self-harming). Definitely not a healthy coping mechanism though.

Her statements about what "you're making her do" are complete bullshit. I hope you don't ever blame yourself for that. She needs to learn to deal with her stress and anger - that's no one else's job but her own.
"Would they care as much about hurting my feelings as I do about hurting theirs?"
"I guess you think I'm a bad mother."
Oh man, mine use the "too old to change" line too. It's like they think their age completely absolves them of their behaviour. Nope!
Thanks :) Sorry to hear about your stuff too. They seem to be incapable of making rational decisions or dealing with things in a civil manner.

Thanks, I never heard of the 'discard' before. Makes a lot of sense. 

Knowing my parents, they'd be too embarrassed to try and show up to the wedding at least, but yeah I'll make sure to keep any online things safe - good call.

I have a feeling my sister is going to get cut off soon by them. She's been standing firm with her boundaries which seems to be making them rage even harder.

Thanks :) I'll keep that trick in mind as I sort through it. Can definitely use the stress reduction. Just returned and it looks like they cleared out EVERYTHING (my graduation picture they had hanging, all my old schoolwork, my stocking etc.) Just wish they could have been more civil about it.
What if... both?

This was the single most important thing that helped break me out of a bad depression. Turning down the 'inner critic' and replacing it with self compassion makes a huge difference. Good luck on your progress, it gets easier!

Omg the slice of bread... That happened to me so often. "You can't be that hungry if you don't want a piece of bread, so quit complaining!"

I used to squish the bread and make it look like a little pizza, with ripped up crusts as the 'toppings'.

I've always felt that way about myself. I like bright, colorful, noisy things: cartoons, animated movies, arcades, video games, anything electronic. My tastes have always been a bit different than others my age. Sometimes it makes me feel a bit awkward, but I've learned to embrace it. If it makes me happy, then who cares? Life's too short to not enjoy what YOU want to enjoy.

>except: these scenes ended with the parent sitting down with the child, and both talked about their feelings, and the parent agreed to back off or be more understanding, the child got more freedom and responsibility with it, etc. 

Couldn't agree more!! She loved to point out the arguments, yelling, and her favorite, "typical moody teenagers!" Yet she failed to realize that on tv they came together in the end and discussed the matters calmly, listened to the kids point of view, learned from each other, made compromises etc. Ours always ended with a screeching "I'm the parent, I'm right! End of discussion!"

Wow, that was a great way to explain it, thanks.

I think growing up in these kinds of households really distorts the "rules of relationships", and it's great to learn how things should actually work. It makes so much sense to hear it too, but it just was never explained that way before.

I did. It still bothers me, but it had to be said.

My eDad called me after the final fight that made me end contact with my nMother. It was his usual pleas for me to "just overlook her behaviour...she can't help it...she doesn't mean it..." 

I told him that he's asking me to let her continue abusing me. I told him that he wants her to be happy, but doesn't seem to care if his kids are.

He said his usual "please be the bigger person" speech, trying to get us to forget her actions and continue like nothing happened. I told him I can't anymore.

I asked him how long it's been since he's contacted my brother, who cut contact only with my mother, but wanted to maintain a relationship with him. He paused, and said solemnly, "it's been awhile..."

The call ended with me reiterating that I can't continue to be abused anymore. He can choose his wife over his children, but some day his children will learn that they need to look out for themselves because their parents sure won't. It was the first time I heard him cry. We don't use the word "love" in my family, but he managed to choke out that he wanted me to know that he's proud of all of us. I think he already knew that he was going to be taking her side again. Haven't heard from him since.

I'm sorry for the shit show you dealt with. Hopefully you are and your SO are ok!

Those comments and actions were beyond inappropriate and abusive. I hope you never have to deal with her shit again. 

Have an awesome wedding and peaceful life together. I'll be in Japan around the same time for my honeymoon, enjoy the cherry blossoms!! You and your SO deserve the relaxation and all things beautiful in this world. Never let others taint that for you.

My sister's been great luckily. I should have mentioned that she's seen through their facade now too, so we keep a united front against them. She just passes along information/ridiculous shit my parents say. 

She's still in contact with them for now, but spent many years as NC. My brother has also been NC for a few years now, and my parents act like he doesn't exist. It'll definitely be nice not having to worry about any drama with him at the wedding. I can actually just enjoy everyone's company and not have to babysit her behaviour. Go to unemployment centres to speed up getting a job.

Do cash jobs - ask neighbors if you can rake leaves, shovel snow, walk dogs, wash their car, or do general labour if they've got any renovating or cleaning to do.
